correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed for exactly three independent Z-valued variables with individual point-mass caps alpha in [1/3,1/2]. Finite mass-cap polytopes reduce to alpha,alpha,beta vertices, and countable supports follow by total-variation approximation. The exact four-term weighted convolution expansion uses representation maxima 7,5,4,3. Equality in the first maximum forces three matching arithmetic progressions; all three heavy-pair counts cannot simultaneously equal four because binary minimal indices would satisfy three impossible pair-sum-one equations. Therefore a weighted deficit min(beta^3,beta delta^2) holds, yielding both exact expressions and an analytically checked switch at 2/5. Explicit independent 3-site laws attain each branch; endpoint degeneracies are permitted. The standalone code at check_concentration.py passed 197568 integer-exact pair optimizations and 81 finite obstruction cases; these are supportive checks, not infinite certificates.

originality.rationale: The exact finite-odd-summand statement is expressly left conjectural in Kurauskas (2026), Conjecture 1.3; prior arbitrary-cap sharp results cover even sums, integer inverse caps and two-atom cases, while the Sperner majorization theorem assumes #-log-concavity absent from all permitted configurations. The exact [1/3,1/2] phase formula and weighted-count incompatibility are not established in inspected primary text. Ten actual targeted published-finding corpus queries and public literature/alias searches found no dominating theorem; this is evidence against known coverage, not a proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: Unindexed publications or specialized results might already prove the same first-fractional three-summand case.
The 2024 interval paper and 2025 variance-rearrangement paper were inspected only to abstract-level; neither is judged decisive coverage on the available descriptions.

value.rationale: The result settles the smallest nontrivial odd summand count across the complete natural first fractional atom-cap interval between the known uniform (1/3) and two-atom (1/2) endpoints of an explicitly stated open signed-concentration problem. The exact value is not a routine known-table extraction: it requires a structural obstruction among competing convolution representation maxima, and identifies a nontrivial change in which orientations attain the universal maximum at alpha=2/5. Neither a general n claim nor a different invariant is needed for its relevance; it provides a sharp small-n benchmark for the larger conjecture.
